insights.claim_template: This book earns more on financial assets than it pays on debt: financial income of {money:financial_income} against financial expense of {money:financial_expense} leaves a net gain of {money:net_financial}, {measure:graded_share} of {money:graded_base}.
insights.formula: Financial income − financial expense, against operating EBITDA

measures.label: Net financial result as a share of ebitda

narrative.explanation: This book earns more on financial assets than it pays on debt: financial income of RON 5,511,010.41 against financial expense of RON 3,092,377.62 leaves a net gain of RON 2,418,632.79, 110.7% of RON 2,185,482.87. Graded critical: the amount at stake is 110.7% of ebitda, against the ladder printed beside this finding. The financial result is graded against the operating earnings it sits beside, because the question is how much of the bottom line the company earned by trading rather than by lending or borrowing.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Separate the operating result from the financial one when judging the trading business. Financial income earned on assets or affiliates does not repeat because trading improved.

insights.claim_template: The net trade float is {money:float}: {money:trade_receivables} owed by customers against {money:trade_payables} owed to suppliers — {measure:dso} of sales outstanding against {measure:dpo} of payables ({money:dpo_payables} of balance-sheet payables over {money:total_operating_expense} of total operating expense, on {measure:period_days}), a gap of {measure:float_days}.
insights.formula: DSO = trade receivables net ÷ revenue × the period's days; DPO = balance-sheet payables ÷ total operating expense × the period's days (the ratio table's one DPO, engine.ratios.table.dpo_days); float = trade receivables net − trade payables

narrative.explanation: The net trade float is RON -6,212,428.22: RON 254,961.33 owed by customers against RON 6,467,389.55 owed to suppliers — 1 day of sales outstanding against 30 days of payables (RON 6,455,119.80 of balance-sheet payables over RON 78,958,595.58 of total operating expense, on 365 days), a gap of -29 days. Graded medium: the amount at stake is 7.9% of revenue, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Trade float is a claim on a year of trading, so it is graded as a share of that year's revenue — the same base both day counts already annualise against.
